**Getting stuck is a documentation bug, not a user error.** This project was written by someone who
already knew where everything was, which is the worst possible position from which to write
instructions. If you had to guess, or search, or give up — that is worth reporting even if you worked
it out in the end.

## Where were you?

<!-- Which document, and which step. A link or a quoted line is perfect. -->

## What happened

<!-- What you ran or clicked, and what came back. Paste the error verbatim if there was one -
     including the boring part before it. -->

## What did you expect?

<!-- Sometimes the step worked exactly as written and still was not what you wanted. That is useful
     too, and it usually means a missing sentence rather than a missing feature. -->

## Your setup

- OS, and whether you are using WSL:
- Building the firmware yourself, or using a release binary:
- Did you have an AI assistant helping (see docs/with-an-assistant.md)? If so, where did it send you
  wrong? That is genuinely useful — those docs are written to be read by assistants too, and if one
  misled you, the page needs fixing.

---

⚠️ **Before you paste:** logs from this project can contain your Wi-Fi network name and your server's
address. Neither is catastrophic, but have a look first — and **never** paste a factory firmware
backup or an NVS dump anywhere, those contain your Wi-Fi password in plain text.
